more_info.overview: Lipases are enzymes that act on fats, including the hydrolysis of fatty-acid glycerides. FDA describes animal lipases extracted from edible stomach or pancreatic tissues and a separate preparation produced by fermentation of Rhizopus niveus. A further specified fungal esterase-lipase is used for flavour development in cheese, fats, oils and milk products. The source, carrier and reaction activity differ between preparations. Consequently, this family name alone does not identify the origin or dietary suitability of a commercial enzyme.
more_info.origin: Source-dependent. FDA describes extracts of edible calf, kid or lamb stomach tissues or pancreatic tissues, as well as separate fungal-fermentation preparations. These are distinct commercial enzyme types.
more_info.uses: Specified lipase preparations are used in fat and oil processing. The fungal esterase-lipase described in 21 CFR 173.140 has flavour-enhancing applications in certain cheeses, fats, oils and milk products.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: Animal-tissue lipases are not suitable for vegans or vegetarians. A microbial source alone does not establish suitability of the whole preparation: the FDA-specified fungal esterase-lipase can use sweet whey as its carrier. Halal and kosher status depends on the particular source, carrier and certification.
